title: Update on Singapore Military's Support to Anti-ISIS Coalition
what_it_is: Update on Singapore Military's Support to Anti-ISIS Coalition

sections.label: SAF deployments to coalition
sections.summary: The SAF deployed a liaison officer, intelligence planner and Imagery Analysis Team, and its tanker aircraft flew 52 sorties refuelling 142 coalition aircraft.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Since December 2014, the SAF has deployed a liaison officer to the US Central Command Headquarters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We have also deployed an intelligence planner since January last year and an Imagery Analysis Team (IAT) since September 2015 to the Combined Joint Task Force (CJTF) Headquarters in Kuwait.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the short period of three months, our tanker aircraft flew 52 sorties and refuelled 142 coalition aircraft.

sections.label: SAF continuing deployments against ISIS
sections.summary: The SAF will continue its 2016 deployments, assessing contributions regularly, as ISIS threats and coordination have increased outside Iraq and Syria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: By contributing to the international effort to tackle the threat at source, we are contributing directly to our own safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And this is the reason why the SAF will continue its deployments throughout 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As the fight against ISIS evolves, we will continue to assess, on a regular basis, the relevance and effectiveness of our contributions and we will work with partners to see how Singapore can best contribute, moving forward, in ways that are within our means and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We recognise that threat levels have gone up, but potential threats, if you like, to various countries have also gone up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: ISIS operatives, as they themselves declare, have become more coordinated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: They said that they have established an arm outside Iraq and Syria and, as you have seen, in the attacks in Paris or even Jakarta, the ability to orchestrate and coordinate has gone up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The threat levels, if you like, to places outside Iraq and Syria have gone up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And, as I have said in 2014, our basis to join the multinational coalition was to protect our Singaporeans here − because we recognise that terrorist attacks will happen.

sections.label: Coalition thanks and home coordination
sections.summary: The coalition is thankful for SAF capabilities, while Singapore reviews plans for better Home Team coordination and SAF contribution to home security.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: They are thankful for our capabilities, how we are able to make sense of various information streams and then package them in a product that is useful to the coalition in terms of identifying areas in which members can use.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But, internally, we are also reviewing our plans to make sure that there is better coordination with the Home Team and to make sure that the SAF is able to contribute to security at home.
